record.original_question: Call a properly edge-colored n-regular graph allowable when it is connected and, for every colors i and j with |i-j| > 1, every walk with color pattern i, j, i, j returns to its starting vertex. Is every allowable graph the symmetry type graph of some maniplex?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Is every allowable graph the symmetry type graph of some maniplex?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A maniplex of rank n is a combinatorial generalization of an abstract polytope, defined as a connected, properly edge-colored n-regular graph M (whose vertices are called flags and whose edge colors come from {0,1,...,n-1}) such that for all colors i, j with |i - j| > 1, every closed walk obtained by alternating colors i, j, i, j has length 4 (equivalently, the i- and j-colored edges form a disjoint union of 4-cycles or double edges). The automorphism group Aut(M) consists of color-preserving graph automorphisms, and it acts freely on the vertex set. The symmetry type graph T(M) of M is the quotient multigraph M/Aut(M), inheriting the edge coloring; it is itself a properly edge-colored n-regular (multi)graph (allowing loops and multiple edges) that is connected and satisfies the same alternating-square condition above.

Call a properly edge-colored n-regular (multi)graph G allowable if:
(i) G is connected, and
(ii) for every pair of colors i, j with |i - j| > 1, every closed walk in G whose edge-color sequence is i, j, i, j returns to its starting vertex (so the subgraph induced by colors i and j is a disjoint union of 4-cycles, double edges, or single edges traversed twice).

Question: Is every allowable graph the symmetry type graph of some maniplex? That is, given an allowable G, does there always exist a maniplex M (of the same rank n) such that T(M) is isomorphic to G as an edge-colored graph?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining whether every premaniplex (equivalently, allowable graph) is the symmetry type graph of some maniplex appears to remain open in general. Partial results are known: every rank-3 premaniplex with at most 2 or 3 vertices is realizable as the symmetry type graph of a maniplex/polytope, and voltage-operation constructions provide further families, but a complete answer for arbitrary rank and arbitrary allowable graphs has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry Type Graphs of Polytopes and Maniplexes
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary conditions are given for a properly edge-colored graph to be the symmetry type graph of a maniplex; such graphs are called premaniplexes.
status_evidence.claim: The realizability question for general premaniplexes is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Voltage Operations on Maniplexes, Polytopes and Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Voltage operations construct maniplexes with prescribed symmetry type graphs, addressing the realizability problem in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial progress toward realizing arbitrary premaniplexes as symmetry type graphs has been made.
